lesson: GIMP is strictly for raster image manipulation. Tasks involving Video editing, Audio, or Vector (SVG) conversion are outside its capabilities.
For precise bulk operations (e.g., batch resizing), scripting (Python/Pillow) is preferred over repetitive GUI actions.
Complex visual effects (filters, specific selection tools) should be performed via GUI to ensure the algorithm matches the tool's specific behavior.
GIMP only supports RGB, Grayscale, and Indexed color modes. CMYK color space is not supported in GIMP.
GIMP can import SVG files and rasterize them, but cannot export to SVG or other vector formats. All GIMP output is raster-based.
GIMP has no built-in web browser or network download functionality. Opening remote images requires downloading them externally first.
GIMP has limited RAW format support and may not open all RAW files. Consider using dedicated RAW converters or check if specific plugins are available.

Image resolution and file size are fundamentally linked - higher resolution requires more pixel data. Enhancing resolution while maintaining or reducing file size is physically constrained by information theory.
GIMP has no built-in GUI for batch processing multiple files. For batch operations, use command-line tools or Python scripts with image libraries like Pillow.
GIMP provides limited UI theme options (Dark/Light/System). Custom color themes or specific color schemes are not available through settings.
